title: Redwood-Constellation marketplace integration tech sync
summary: High-level technical sync to align Redwood and Constellation on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint solution (Redwood Dedicated + Constellation marketplace delivery), and next steps for integration tests and security review.
action_items: Samir Patel - share initial reference architecture diagram (Terraform + Helm flow) - due 2026-04-13
Priya Kapoor - provide Constellation's marketplace packaging checklist and entitlements schema - due 2026-04-09
Lucia Gomez - run a short validation benchmark (1 GPU, 512 token LLM workload) and share perf numbers - due 2026-04-15
Daniel Park - send security control matrix and clarify KMS integration constraints - due 2026-04-12
Oliver Reed - confirm preferred billing model (metered vs. seat) and mapping to Redwood usage events - due 2026-04-10
next_steps: Redwood to upload draft reference-arch doc to shared drive
Constellation to return marketplace checklist and required artifacts
Schedule partner security review (2nd week of April)
One-week follow-up to review benchmark results and finalize packaging approach
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we got most of the folks. um quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Maya here, thanks Samir.
[00:08] Oliver Reed: Oliver on from Constellation.
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Priya here. Daniel joining in a bit.
[00:14] Lucia Gomez: Lucia from Redwood SE team. Samir, Aisha also on.
[00:18] Samir Patel: perfect. goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing requirements and the joint reference architecture - specifically how we would package Redwood Dedicated as a marketplace offer on Constellation, and options for private deployments and AMI/VM vs container marketplace listings.
[00:32] Oliver Reed: yes, we want to make sure the listing meets our entitlements model. for example, we have metered usage and also we support a reserved sku. curious how Redwood maps metrics for billing.
[00:42] Lucia Gomez: right, on Redwood side we emit usage events per-request and token-level aggregates; we can map to metered units or convert to reserved units via a multiplier. there might be some normalization but it’s doable. sometimes names in the telemetry get weird - we call it kv cache events in the runtime logs, may show up as kv_hits in the payload.
[00:58] Priya Kapoor: ok good. from packaging perspective, Constellation supports three listing types: container image (Helm chart), AMI/VM image, and a managed SaaS listing. we need to know what Redwood will provide.
[01:10] Samir Patel: we can provide a Helm chart and a hardened AMI. for managed SaaS we’d want to integrate SSO and service-to-service auth hooks with your marketplace. also need to confirm if you require a private VPC flow or if partners can use marketplace-managed network.
[01:26] Maya Chen: most enterprise customers choose marketplace-managed but some regulated customers require VPC peering or bring-your-own-VPC. listing should call out both options.
[01:34] Daniel Park: (joins) sorry for the delay, Daniel Park, security. quick question: how does Redwood handle KMS and customer keying for private deployments?
[01:41] Aisha Rahman: hi Daniel. in Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; our deployment templates allow passing in KMS ARN or key id at deploy time. for hosted we manage keys but we offer CMKs wrapped in our HSM per enterprise contracts. there’s sometimes confusion in naming in our docs - we call it key-wrap, keys-provider, etc - we’ll make sure to standardize the language.
[02:02] Daniel Park: ok we’ll need a security control matrix and an explanation of audit logs for the marketplace listing.
[02:08] Samir Patel: yes we’ll prepare that. also worth calling out SOC2 and ISO statuses - Redwood is SOC2 Type II and working toward ISO 27001 (note: transcription may have that wrong in some docs).
[02:20] Oliver Reed: for the reference architecture, we want to show a flow where a Constellation customer can click purchase -> deploys AMI into their account or spins up from our managed SaaS offering which then talks to Redwood Dedicated pools. how does Redwood route requests between hosted and dedicated?
[02:36] Lucia Gomez: good question. we have a smart routing layer; policy can route by region, latency, or cost. for example a customer can pin to Dedicated capacity or fall back to hosted if quota exceeded. for marketplace we’d recommend a canary deployment and an entitlement token exchange.
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: can we get an example of the entitlement token exchange? we need to ensure the marketplace issues a token that Redwood will accept and map to account in our portal.
[02:58] Samir Patel: yes, we can do JWT-based entitlements that include sku + expiry + org id; Redwood validates signature against Constellation marketplace public keys and maps to account id. there are edge cases - if token expired we fallback to a grace policy rather than failing outright.
[03:15] Maya Chen: good. what about observability? customers will expect per-route dashboards and traces for billing disputes.
[03:22] Lucia Gomez: Redwood Console exposes per-route cost/latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. for marketplace we can expose a limited read-only role to Constellation operators if required, or export logs via your log-forwarding. logs include tokenized account id and usage events but we can mask PII.
[03:37] Daniel Park: that helps. how about the benchmark we discussed - what baseline are we running?
[03:42] Samir Patel: plan is a 1 GPU baseline, 512 token request distribution, 80/20 short/long tail, measure p50/p90 latency and tokens/sec and also memory/kv cache hit rate. Lucia will run it on a sample model.
[03:55] Lucia Gomez: yes I’ll run that on our test cluster; expectation is p50 sub-200ms for short prompts on T4-class equivalent but we’ll provide exact numbers. note noise in multi-tenant hosted envs can vary.
[04:07] Priya Kapoor: for the marketplace listing we also need a reference arch doc that shows network flows, firewall rules, required IAM roles, and terraform snippets. do you have a starter repo?
[04:18] Aisha Rahman: we have a partner repo with terraform modules and a Helm chart. we’ll share the repo link. caveat: some of the module variables names changed last quarter so we’ll tag a stable release for the marketplace packaging.
[04:31] Oliver Reed: great, please include a minimal example that deploys Redwood Dedicated into a customer account with a sample workload and a smoke test.
[04:39] Samir Patel: yep we’ll include smoke tests. also we should clarify support SLAs: what level does Constellation expect for marketplace managed offers?
[04:47] Maya Chen: standard marketplace partners offer 24x7 for P1 with 1 hour initial response and extended enterprise can choose premium support. we want to document escalation paths in the listing.
[04:57] Samir Patel: understood. Redwood can provide escalation docs and we’ll include on-call contacts for the integration period.
[05:03] Priya Kapoor: a couple of technical concerns - stateful data, customer data residency and log retention. some customers require logs to stay in-region and never leave account.
[05:14] Lucia Gomez: for private deployments data never leaves customer VPC. for hosted flows we have region-based storage and retention policies. we can add hooks to ship logs to customer log storage if required.
[05:26] Daniel Park: also need to confirm encryption at rest for KV cache and model checkpoints.
[05:31] Aisha Rahman: yes encrypted at rest, we use disk encryption with customer-managed keys for Private and our managed keys for hosted unless customer overrides. we’ll document checkpoint storage details.
[05:42] Oliver Reed: thinking about joint marketing, we’ll want a reference-arch diagram and a short doc for the marketplace detail section. is there an existing template?
[05:49] Samir Patel: Redwood has a partner reference-arch template we can adapt to Constellation’s listing format. we’ll produce that as a living doc in the shared drive.
[05:58] Maya Chen: timeline-wise, marketplace listing targeted for May pilot with a handful of customers in June. does that align?
[06:05] Samir Patel: sounds doable. main blockers: finalize entitlements mapping, security sign-off, and benchmark results.
[06:12] Lucia Gomez: I’ll aim to run benchmark by 2026-04-15 and post results.
[06:17] Priya Kapoor: I’ll get the packaging checklist over by next Thursday.
[06:21] Daniel Park: I’ll assemble the security questions and flag anything unusual.
[06:25] Samir Patel: great. quick note on the reference arch - we should call out fallback policies and canary routing in the diagram. some customers like to see automatic failover to regional hosted endpoints.
[06:36] Aisha Rahman: also include quantization/compatibility notes - some market models may require specific runtimes or kernel builds. we’ll note recommended CPU/GPU profiles.
[06:46] Oliver Reed: any known gaps?
[06:48] Lucia Gomez: only that some of our marketplace packaging scripts need a minor update to handle Constellation’s entitlement token header naming; small change.
[06:55] Samir Patel: ok we’ll make that change and tag a release.
[06:58] Maya Chen: can we recap next steps?
[07:00] Samir Patel: sure - Samir will upload reference arch draft; Lucia runs benchmark; Priya shares checklist; Daniel sends security matrix; Oliver confirms billing model. we’ll meet again in one week.
[07:14] Oliver Reed: yep, thanks everyone.
[07:16] Priya Kapoor: thanks.
[07:17] Lucia Gomez: thanks all.
[07:18] (call ends)
